text:
alex: Heads up — saw a perf regression on master after the kernel-selector change. Multi-GPU Llama-13B (tp=2, pp=1) synthetic 8k seq run: token throughput down ~22% and end-to-end latency p95 up ~30%.

maria: ugh. any quick perf markers or profiler snaps?

alex: pasted a short flame snippet from our lightweight tracer:
```
wall: total 1000ms
compute kernels: 640ms
all-reduce/comm: 320ms  <-- moved up from ~220ms baseline
other: 40ms
```

ryan: that jump smells like NCCL algo/proto or channel count change. We recently switched kernel selector heuristics to prefer the "proto" path for small collectives to reduce kernel divergence. Might be increasing number of smaller allreduces.

alex: Exactly. I also saw an increase in number of NCCL collectives in the profile (counts doubled for small reductions). KV cache behaviour and prefix batching might be increasing num small reductions per step.

sophie: Can you share the collector output from /tmp/nccl_profile.txt? Also what NCCL envs were in CI?

alex: quick dump:
```
NCCL_PROTO=1
NCCL_ALGO=2
NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD=8192
NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
```
Profile snippet: many <bytes<8k> collectives show proto fallback and serial ordering.

perf-bot: Deploy 2026-03-15T09:12 by alex — kernel-selector change (PR #5123) — smoke passed.

maria: hypothesis: kernel-selector now favors a quantized kernel variant that reduces compute but fragments the comm pattern, causing more small-sized allreduces (worse wire efficiency). We should test toggling LL/LL128 and increasing the LL threshold.

ryan: Agreed. Try these env experiments locally:
```
# force LL128-like path and bigger coalescing
export NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD=16384
export NCCL_PROTO=2   # try proto=LL128/tuning path
export NCCL_ALGO=ring # explicit guarded test
export NCCL_BUFFSIZE=2097152
```
Also run with NCCL_DEBUG=WARN to keep logs readable.

alex: ran quick A/B — setting NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD=16384 cut comm time from 320ms -> 260ms, throughput back to ~95% of baseline. Still ~5% gap.

sophie: good signal. Next: check whether batching heuristic triggers more small sends due to prefix-KV cache misses. Could be our batching window emits more interleaved small tensors.

alex: I instrumented batching: average batch size per step dropped from 12 -> 8 micro-batches after selector change, so more frequent allreduces.

maria: action items then: (1) add a safeguard in kernel selector to prefer coalescing of small comm ops when total comm bytes per step > X, (2) run a controlled experiment toggling NCCL_PP/CHANNELS variants, (3) add microbenchmark to CI that asserts allreduce count/bytes don't regress >10%.

ryan: for (2) I'll run channel experiments — NCCL channel tuning was promising before. I'll test multi-channel and LL128 toggles across 4/8 GPU sharded runs.

sophie: Also add KV-cache hotpath metric: cache hit ratio + average kv batch size per step to the perf dashboard. That'll catch regressions earlier.

alex: I'll revert the kernel-selector change on a rollback branch and run full perf suite vs the env-tuned experiments to confirm root cause.

perf-bot: Perf job queued: compare/selector-rollback vs master — job id 8672.

maria: thanks. if anyone lands quick kernel tweaks, ping me — I'd like to validate model quality (we're changing kernel choices, could affect numerics).

alex: noted. I'll post results from the rollback vs tuned-NCCL run here when job finishes.

ryan: tagging @infra-bot to reserve 8xA100 for the channel sweep tomorrow morning.

infra-bot: reserving 8xA100 cluster from 2026-03-16 06:00-09:00 UTC for team "eng-runtime" — reservation id r-4492.

sophie: nice. also let's add a small unit test: synthetic allreduce coalescing simulation so future kernel selector changes have a guard.

alex: agreed. temporary mitigation: set NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD=16384 in the dedicated CI perf runner until root cause is fixed.

maria: summary: regression likely due to selector-induced fragmentation causing more small allreduces. Mitigations = NCCL tuning (LL threshold, LL128/proto path, buffer sizes), selector change revert + improved coalescing heuristics, KV cache metrics and CI guard.

alex: +1 — will follow up with numbers. thanks all :thumbsup:
